points.text: 1 individuals (within a population) can, breed / mate / reproduce ;
2 to produce fertile offspring ;
3 are reproductively isolated (from other species) / AW ;
any one from:
1 for organisms that, do not breed sexually / are asexual ;
2 for, fossil / extinct, organisms ;
3 morphological differences are easier to determine ;
4 often not possible to observe reproductive behaviour ;
5 time required for mating behaviour may take too long (to be observed) / not possible to achieve conditions in which mating can occur (while being observed) ;
any four from:
max three:
1 both are prokaryotes or both have no, nucleus / (double) membrane-bound organelles ;
2 both have circular DNA ;
3 both have 70S ribosomes ;
4 both reproduce by, binary fission / budding / fragmentation ;
max three:
5 bacteria cell wall made of peptidoglycan whereas Archaea cell wall does not have peptidoglycan ;
6 bacteria cell membrane has ester-linked lipids whereas Archaea cell membrane has ether-linked lipids ;
7 have different ribosomal RNA ;
8 Bacteria do not have (DNA associated with) histones whereas Archaea do have (DNA associated with) histones ;
9 Bacteria form spores whereas Archaea do not form spores ;
